# `start_exposure`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start capture in the current exposure mode, optionally selecting the frame type.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe6620, StartExposure @0x2130a0 (64-bit build) |

Requires an open camera. In exposure mode 0 an optional type (light, dark, bias, flat; case-insensitive) selects the frame type before starting; the type change is kept even if a later step fails. Depending on the existing exposure mode the device starts single, continuous or sequence capture on a named worker thread asynchronously; the reply result 0 acknowledges the start, not completion. No exposure time or bin is read here (see set_camera_exp_and_bin). Mode 1 may release buffers, set exposure and set the video subframe before starting video.

Side effects: Changes the frame selection and reconnect state and starts capture work on a worker thread; may release buffers and set exposure and subframe in video mode.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_exposure"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Optional. Either an object with the members below, or an array whose first element is the frame type string (keep_autosave_dev has no array form). Scalar or wrong top-level types and an empty array behave as absent params and use the defaults. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | A three-point polar alignment is working | `not supported` |
| 106 | keep_autosave_dev present with a type other than boolean or integer | `expected bool param` |
| 105 | type present and not a string (exposure mode 0) | `expected string param` |
| 209 | type non-empty but not a recognised frame name | `invalid value` |
| 318 | Camera is not open | `device not connected` |
| 206 | An exposure or capture flag is set or the capture thread is active | `capture is active` |
| 524 | Planet stacking is active | `function conflict` |
| 102 | Exposure mode 3 | `invalid params` |
| 208 | Sequence disk-space check fails (required size plus 150) | `disk is full` |
| 207 | Operation failure whose thread-local error code is zero (the default substituted when the callee set none); other callee-set codes are forwarded unchanged | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Plan-size, video-start and thread-creation failures below StartExposure are propagated with their own codes and are not enumerated by the source.

## Example

Request, light:

```json
{"id":29,"method":"start_exposure","params":{"type":"light","keep_autosave_dev":false}}
```

Request, positional:

```json
{"id":30,"method":"start_exposure","params":["dark"]}
```

Request, bare:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"start_exposure"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_exposure","result":0,"code":0,"id":29}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_exposure","error":"capture is active","code":206,"id":32}
```
